title: A Thousand Mountains | If I Were Not Me
subtitle: The original song comes from Almost a Comedy—a clichéd story with tears amid laughter, but I like it.
body:
If it were not autumn If there were no fallen leaf Pressed against my chest by the wind Willful and absurd If I were not me If I had sent only the postcard The ginkgo leaf hidden in the envelope Decaying and brilliant
Do not look back, my dear girl And please do not sing softly to me again How I wish to gaze into your eyes once more But I cannot do this You say, one of a kind But you and I both know It was only because I caught that leaf Not because it was special
Do not be sad, my dear girl Do not worry that my world is dim and lightless I used to love imagining leaning on your shoulder But I cannot do this How I wish to brush away the furrows between your brows To replace vows to the mountains with a steadfast embrace But I cannot do this Cannot do this
If I were not me If fish could sing too I would surely stay by your side And not let you grieve If I were not me If trees could fly too I would surely stay by your side And not let you be hurt If I were not me What would happen then?
